final_candidates.decision_summary: S16E acts as a phosphomimetic in the N-terminal transactivation domain, facilitating CycT1/CDK9 interaction and promoting Tat-mediated transcription.
K28R preserves positive charge while preventing repressive post-translational modifications at K28, enhancing TAR RNA binding and transactivation.
K50R in the basic arginine-rich motif preserves high affinity TAR RNA binding and maintains nuclear localization.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 candidates are optimized for Tat transactivation efficiency based on domain function analysis.

history.rationale: Glutamate substitution at Ser16 acts as a phosphomimetic that enhances Tat activation domain interaction with host transcription factors and boosts transactivation efficiency.
S16E acts as a phosphomimetic in the N-terminal domain, promoting positive transactivation dynamics and CycT1/CDK9 interaction.
Arginine substitution at Lys28 preserves basic charge while optimizing PCAF interaction dynamics and P-TEFb complex recruitment.
K28R preserves positive charge while preventing transient inactivation, maintaining high affinity for TAR RNA and elongation complexes.
Arginine substitution at Lys50 maintains electrostatic interactions required for TAR RNA binding while preventing early inactivation by acetylation.
K50R in the basic ARM region locks the arginine-rich motif in a basic state, enhancing RNA binding and nuclear localization.
Valine-to-isoleucine substitution at position 36 is a well-characterized natural variant that improves core hydrophobic packing and transactivation.
V36I provides conservative hydrophobic packing optimization in the core domain, stabilizing overall protein fold.
Arginine substitution at Lys51 stabilizes the basic arginine-rich motif binding to TAR RNA and enhances transactivation capability.
K51R stabilizes basic interactions within the ARM region with TAR RNA while maintaining structural integrity.
Arginine substitution at Lys41 maintains core domain structural integrity and optimizes interaction with Cyclin T1 in the P-TEFb complex.
K41R maintains core basicity and structural stability without disrupting transactivation complex assembly.
Lysine substitution at position 24 introduces positive charge near the cysteine-rich region, facilitating host factor recruitment.
N24K introduces additional positive electrostatic potential near the Cys-rich region to aid binding interactions.
Arginine substitution at Lys29 maintains positive charge density near the core region and protects against degrading ubiquitination.
K29R maintains positive charge near the Tat core/ARM junction.
Glutamate substitution at Ser46 mimics regulatory phosphorylation at the core-ARM boundary, promoting functional transactivation complex formation.
S46E provides phosphomimetic character in the core region, though potential local structural disruption lowers confidence.
Basic lysine substitution at position 9 enhances electrostatic surface potential of the N-terminal domain to promote functional co-factor assembly.
E9K alters N-terminal charge distribution, potentially influencing cellular uptake and transactivation efficiency.
